To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) anti-malware vendors have improved their detection performances in the last two years; (ii) anti-mal-ware engines still fail to detect obfuscated malware; (iii) anti-mal-ware systems search for possible malicious code in the assets of the Android application; (iv) anti-malicious engines are able to detect malware even in the absence of malicious code; (v) anti-malwares engines are still not robust enough against more complex obfuscation techniques;

the detection performance of anti-malwares has improved in recent years, but it is still far from perfect and that the use of obfuscation techniques is still a viable strategy for Android malware developers.
• The obfuscation of Android malware has a limited effect on the detection performances of most anti-malware products.
